verdict.rationale: LlamaParse documents its own path from tables to structured output: Extract returns JSON matching a user-defined schema, table row extraction handles repeating entities, and Parse examples pull every table into pandas DataFrames with page provenance. That covers the core of turning tables into typed rows or JSON. There is no evidence that the output loads into a database without manual cleanup, and one hands-on user found table numbers were not returned in tabular form, which lowers confidence. missing for 10: evidence that output is cleanly typed and database-load-ready without post-processing, any database loader or sink for extracted rows, independent hands-on confirmation of schema-conformant table-row accuracy.

support.subject: As a data engineer, I turn extracted tables into typed rows/JSON I can load into a database without manual cleanup
